Naji Marshall and Walter Clayton should also get a boost in minutes and playmaking responsibilities off the bench.

news.headline: Irving (knee) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Celtics.
news.story: Irving poured in a game-high 34 points in 37 minutes during Saturday's 127-117 loss to Cleveland, so there's a decent chance Dallas will give its star point guard the night off for the second leg of their back-to-back set. If he is indeed out, Cooper Flagg's usage would see a massive boost while Naji Marshall and Walter Clayton Jr. would figure to earn more minutes off the bench.

news.headline: Fantasy risers and fallers: Pelicans' Fears provides hope; Harden's numbers down
Fears registered 19 points (6-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-7 FT), 10 rebounds and 10 assists across 29 minutes in Monday's 115-94 victory over the Warriors.
news.story: Fears put together a memorable performance, recording the first triple-double of his young career in a winning effort. After scoring in single digits in the first two games of the campaign, the guard has reached double figures in 13 straight contests. Overall, Fears is averaging 15.5 points, 5.5 assists, 4.9 rebounds and 1.0 steals while starting all 15 games this season.

news.headline: Peterson logged 13 points (3-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 5-7 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal in 31 minutes during Tuesday's 132-107 victory over the Clippers.
news.story: Peterson never found his shooting touch, but he still finished with a decent total as the Jazz snapped their long losing streak. The No. 2 overall pick has been one of the few bright spots in a rough start for the club, averaging 17.1 points as a rookie. With Lauri Markkanen (hand) and Jaren Jackson (knee) sidelined, Peterson should continue to get a heavy share of the offense.

news.headline: Peterson recorded 17 points (7-20 FG, 3-9 3Pt), five rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal over 34 minutes during Sunday's 110-102 loss to San Antonio.
news.story: Peterson didn't deliver his most efficient shooting performance in Sunday's loss. However, the rookie guard still finished as Utah's second-leading scorer while chipping in multiple combined steals-plus-blocks for a third straight game. He's scored at least 17 points in six straight games, during which he's averaged 23.2 points, 4.7 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.0 blocks in 32.8 minutes per showing.

Acuff ended with 26 points (10-25 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 3-4 FT) and six assists over 33 minutes during Sunday's 125-103 loss to Oklahoma City.
news.story: It was another high-volume performance from the seventh overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. Acuff has scored more than 20 points in eight of the last nine games, averaging 27.2 points, 8.1 assists, 3.9 boards, 3.7 threes and 1.1 steals in 37.4 minutes over that stretch, and his shooting is beginning to improve as well. He's shot 44.1 percent from the floor over that span and 37.1 percent from three-point range.
